gap_notes: CORE cannot be scored yet: ingested sources are still classical only (Ptolemy, Lilly, Valens). Psychological, living-traditional, and professional schools pending.

Valens I.1 is a topical/significator catalog (sect, colour, taste, body parts), not Ptolemy/Lilly elemental qualities. Do not backfill heat/cold/dry/moist from Valens, and do not average catalogs into function.
Benefic status conflict: Ptolemy calls the Sun of common influence with whatever it joins; Lilly says it is equivalent to a fortune if well dignified. Do not collapse to one polarity lemma.
Object-level themes mix compared and school_specific lemmas. Per-lemma evidence_tier stays in this ledger; knowledge-object schema is not expanded for that.
Layer 1 requires positive_expression; it is filled from Lilly well-dignified manners only until a second school class is compared. Valens is still source_class=classical.

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XI Manners when well dignified (1659 p.70)
claims.original_claim: When well dignified: faithful, punctual, desirous to rule, prudent, majestic, industrious of honour, deliberate in speech, affable.
claims.normalized_claim: Dignified Sun: faithful, commanding, honour-seeking, deliberate

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XI When ill dignified (1659 p.70)
claims.original_claim: When ill: arrogant, proud, disdainful, restless, domineering, expensive, a spendthrift who thinks others bound to him.
claims.normalized_claim: Debilitated Sun: arrogance, pride, wasteful domination

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XI Motion (1659 p.69)
claims.original_claim: The Sun finishes the zodiac in one year; always direct, never retrograde.
